errorCodes.meaning: No account with this id exists in the named context that the caller may see. See the family conventions §2.
The account is `suspended` or `archived` and cannot be used.
The caller is not the consumer of any binding on this account.

The request uses the shape the account's model does not take: `presign` for a model that issues sessions or tokens, which can bind neither an operation, a length nor a checksum into what it issues; or `scope` for `s3-static-presign`, which in this version issues only presigned requests. `details.expected` names the shape the model takes.

The presign batch breaks a rule its schema cannot state: an `uploadId` missing for an operation that needs one, present beside `create-multipart`, two identical operations, or two `upload-part` operations naming the same part.

The requested scope is not inside the binding's ceiling: a prefix no ceiling prefix begins, an action the ceiling lacks, or — for `presign` — an operation whose required ceiling action the ceiling lacks.

The presign batch is valid, but its sealed answer would exceed the bound on `sealedCredential` (262144 characters). The custodian refuses it rather than truncate the set or answer over the bound, and it does not count against the binding's rate. `details.maxOperations`, when the custodian gives it, is a count of the batch's first operations, taken in order, whose answer is certain to fit if they are asked for alone; it may be lower than the most that would fit, and it is a statement about these operations only. The caller splits the batch and asks again, and handles another `responseTooLarge` on any part.
The binding's rate is exhausted. `details.retryAfterSeconds` says when to try again.
The account cannot be used until its provider-side setup is redone: after a restore that could not carry its key or secret, or while a rotation awaits confirmation.
The provider refused the custodian's request. `details.providerError` carries the provider's words, verbatim, truncated, with any credential removed.
The provider could not be reached or did not answer in time.
The account is `sui-signer`, which issues no credentials; use external/sign.
The caller's DID offers no X25519 key-agreement key to seal the credential to: it is not a `did:key`, and its resolved DID document has no X25519 `keyAgreement` verification method.

AccountContextId.description: The custodian context that owns the account. Act scope in this context decides who may manage the account and who may consume it; the account's keys are derived in this context's key space.
AccountContextId.title: AccountContextId

AccountId.description: The account's identifier within its context, chosen by whoever creates it. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, so that it can be embedded in a certificate subject, a token subject or a provider-side condition without escaping. Unique per context; never reused after deletion while anything that names it (a provider-side trust policy, an audit row) may still exist.
AccountId.title: AccountId

ChecksumSha256.description: A SHA-256 digest in standard base64 (RFC 4648 §4, padded), as S3 carries it in `x-amz-checksum-sha256`.
ChecksumSha256.title: ChecksumSha256

CredentialScope.description: What one issuance may do. For storage models, `prefix` and `actions` (both required, a rule this schema leaves to the custodian because other models use neither); for `s3-static-presign`, also `objectKey`, since a presigned URL is one operation on one object; for `oauth2-private-key-jwt`, `scopes`.

objectKey.description: `s3-static-presign` only: the object's name within `prefix`. The presigned URL names `prefix` + `objectKey` and nothing else, and `actions` must hold exactly one action.

CredentialScope.title: CredentialScope

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

PresignBatch.description: `s3-static-presign` only: up to 64 operations on **one** object, `prefix` + `objectKey`, and at most one multipart upload of it. Each operation becomes one presigned request, sealed together. Consistency rules JSON Schema cannot state, which the custodian enforces: `uploadId` is present exactly when an operation needs it (`upload-part`, `list-parts`, `complete-multipart`, `abort-multipart`) and absent when the batch holds `create-multipart`; no two operations are identical; no two `upload-part` operations name the same `partNumber`.

objectKey.description: The object's name within `prefix`. Every request in the batch names `prefix` + `objectKey` and no other object.

requests.description: At most 64. Each presigned request is bearer authority until it expires, so a batch holds what a consumer can use within its lifetime; a larger upload asks again, or writes larger parts. A batch whose sealed answer would exceed `sealedCredential`'s bound is refused with `responseTooLarge`, whatever its count.

uploadId.description: The multipart upload the batch's multipart operations act on, as storage returned it from CreateMultipartUpload. Signed into each such request's query, percent-encoded by the SigV4 encoder, never interpolated.

PresignBatch.title: PresignBatch

PresignRequest.description: One operation to presign, discriminated by `operation`. The ceiling action each needs is in `PresignOperation`.

oneOf.description: PutObject of the whole object, bound to its exact length and SHA-256.

contentLength.description: The object's exact length in bytes, signed into the request as `Content-Length`. At most 5 GiB, S3's single-request ceiling.

oneOf.title: PresignPut

oneOf.description: HeadObject, with `x-amz-checksum-mode: ENABLED` signed so storage reports the object's checksum.
oneOf.title: PresignHead

oneOf.description: CreateMultipartUpload, with `x-amz-checksum-algorithm: SHA256` signed so every part of the upload must carry a SHA-256 checksum.
oneOf.title: PresignCreateMultipart

oneOf.description: UploadPart of one part of `uploadId`, bound to its number, its exact length and its SHA-256.

contentLength.description: The part's exact length in bytes, signed into the request as `Content-Length`. At most 5 GiB, S3's part ceiling.

oneOf.title: PresignUploadPart

oneOf.description: ListParts of `uploadId`: each part's number, length, ETag and checksum, up to 1000 per page.

partNumberMarker.description: List parts after this number. Absent, from the first.

oneOf.title: PresignListParts

oneOf.description: CompleteMultipartUpload of `uploadId`, bound to the assembled object's exact length.

contentLength.description: The assembled object's exact length in bytes, signed into the request as `x-amz-mp-object-size`, so storage refuses a completion that would assemble any other size. At most 5 TiB, S3's object ceiling.

oneOf.title: PresignCompleteMultipart

PresignRequest.title: PresignRequest

ProviderObjectAction.description: `put`: write an object. `get`: read one. `delete`: remove one. No list, ACL, policy or bucket-level action exists here, so none can be granted.
ProviderObjectAction.title: ProviderObjectAction

ProviderObjectPrefix.description: An object-key prefix within the account's bucket: one or more segments of lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, each beginning with a letter or digit and ending with `/`. No quote, backslash, wildcard, whitespace, `..` segment or empty segment can appear. That is deliberate: the custodian places this value inside a provider policy — an IAM session policy (JSON), a GCS Credential Access Boundary condition (CEL) — and a value able to carry a metacharacter can break out of the string it is placed in and widen the policy. That is a known class of defect (CVE-2026-42811, a CEL injection in downscoped GCS credentials). Even with this pattern, a custodian MUST build provider policies with the provider language's own encoder, never by string interpolation.
ProviderObjectPrefix.title: ProviderObjectPrefix

expiresAt.description: The provider's expiry for the credential, in the clear; for `presign`, the earliest expiry in the batch.

presign.description: The batch actually presigned, which equals the requested one.

scope.description: The scope actually granted, which equals the requested one.

sealedCredential.description: A `SealedTransferBundle` (external/_shared/0.1), sealed to the caller's key-agreement key, whose cleartext is an `ExternalCredentialPayload` for `scope` or a `PresignedRequestSet` for `presign`. Bounded at 256 KiB rather than the shared 64 KiB because a batch of presigned requests does not fit 64 KiB. A custodian never answers above this bound and never truncates the set: a batch whose sealed set would not fit is refused with `responseTooLarge`.
sealedCredential.pattern: ^-----BEGIN VTA SEALED BUNDLE-----[\s\S]+-----END VTA SEALED BUNDLE-----\s*$

schema.description: Obtain a short-lived, downscoped provider credential from an external account, sealed to the caller: session or token credentials under `scope`, or a batch of presigned requests on one object under `presign`. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

scope.description: For every brokered model but `s3-static-presign`: the prefix and actions, or the OAuth scopes, the session or token is downscoped to. `objectKey` is not used in this version.

ttlSeconds.description: Requested lifetime; never more than the binding's `maxTtlSeconds`. For `presign`, the lifetime of every URL in the batch.

schema.title: External Credentials — Issue — payload
